examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: CIDR blocks must be aligned to their prefix length and contain a power-of-two number of addresses. Longest-prefix matching chooses the most specific matching route, not the first table row. Compute host ranges by applying the mask, and distinguish total addresses from ordinarily assignable hosts.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
How many ordinary assignable host addresses occur in an IPv4 /26 subnet?

**Answer: 62.** There are 32−26=6 host bits, giving 64 addresses. Reserving network and broadcast addresses leaves 64−2=62 ordinary host addresses.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
The minus-two convention has special cases such as /31 point-to-point links. Apply the question's network model rather than subtracting blindly.

CIDR blocks must start on a boundary aligned with their block size.
